conventions.convention: Positive Artin crossings act on fusion morphisms by inverse precomposition. Generator matrices are T_i^{-1} R_i T_i; products act right-to-left on column vectors, reversing chronological order.

An encoding is an isometry J from a positive-dimensional computational space into a nonzero fixed-total fusion space; P=JJ* projects onto its image. The code subspace is not identified with a categorical object.
Logical block error is ||PWP−JUJ*|| and leakage amplitude is ||(I−P)WP||. JUJ* is zero on the complement, whereas ambient approximation targets use unitary complement blocks.
Projective distance minimizes over one common unit scalar. Independent phases in different total-charge blocks are not permitted.

The six-anyon code requires both consecutive triples to have total charge τ, with ordered local paths (1,1), (1,τ), (τ,1), (τ,τ). Its dimensions are four in ambient dimensions five and eight; the complementary dimensions are one and four.
The Fibonacci relative exchange phase is r=exp(−3πi/5), with the displayed real F block. Path labels 0 and 1 mean the unit and τ, respectively, and paths include x_0 through x_6.
The exact specialization sends r to 15, r^{-1} to 29, φ to 19, and the positive square root of φ to 9 in F_31. Complex conjugation is performed in the number field before reduction.
The all-adjacent-pair Majorana identification and relative phase i are explicit interface hypotheses. The three-anyon Ising sector does not establish this identification for arbitrary m.

Density and covering results assume ACω through the stated Lie-group suppliers. Arbitrary-register universality is an existence claim with uniform spectator bounds and no useful joint braid-length or search-time bound.

load_bearing.statement: Assume ACω. For the normalized simultaneous six-τ Fibonacci B6 representation on V(τ^6→1)⊕V(τ^6→τ)≅C^5⊕C^8, the closure in U(5)×U(8) contains SU(5)×SU(8).

For the stated Fibonacci path bases and fixed-chirality F/R data, P_i=φ^{-1}E_i are orthogonal projections of ranks two and three, satisfy P_iP_{i+1}P_i=φ^{-2}P_i and distant commutation, and B_i=rI+(1−r)P_i are unitary Artin representations with determinants r^3 and r^5.
For r=exp(−3πi/5), φ=1−r−r^{-1}, and s=√φ>0, the stated two monic relations present Z[r,s], and r↦15, r^{-1}↦29, φ↦19, s↦9 defines a homomorphism to F_31.
Assume ACω. In the normalized Fibonacci B6 representation on V(τ^6→1)≅C^5, the closure of the braid image in U(5) contains SU(5).
Assume ACω. In the normalized Fibonacci B6 representation on V(τ^6→τ)≅C^8, the closure of the braid image in U(8) contains SU(8).

Assume ACω, n≥2, and c∈{1,τ} with V(τ^n→c) nonzero. For any adjacent pair of encoded triples, U∈U(4), and δ>0, one normalized six-strand braid is within δ of a code-preserving ideal extension on the entire V(τ^{3n}→c), giving uniform logical-error and leakage bounds over spectators and arbitrary ambient inputs.
Assume ACω. The projective Fibonacci generators on the two-dimensional three-τ, total-τ fusion space generate a subgroup dense in PU(2).
For an orthogonal decomposition V=PV⊕(I−P)V and unitary block target T=U⊕W, any ambient unitary G satisfying ||G−T||≤δ has logical block error relative to U and leakage amplitude both at most δ.

For ideal code-preserving unitaries W_j and physical unitaries V_j with ||V_j−W_j||≤δ_j, the product error, logical block error, and leakage amplitude are bounded by the sum of δ_j; empty products are I and the empty sum is zero.

For generator normalization by the common Fibonacci exchange scalar R_1, ρ(b)=R_1^{e(b)}ρ̃(b) on every total-charge block and spectator multiplicity. Under coherent control the scalar is relative and must be tracked.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.2 says that applying the same Lie-word operations to (X_5,X_8) gives elements of the joint Lie algebra, but membership of this initial pair is not stated or justified. Steps 1.1 and 2.1 supply the common irrational eigenangle, so a reader can obtain the simultaneous circle as the closure of powers of (C_5,C_8), whose tangent is proportional to (C_5−C_5^{-1},C_8−C_8^{-1}). Separate projection density alone would not justify this step. Both cited certificate scripts were run and reproduced determinants 17 and 22 modulo 31.

Proof 2.1 passes from the categorical tensor-power action to 'restriction to V(x^n→c)'. This V is a Hom multiplicity space, not literally an object summand of the tensor power. The required induced action is f↦f∘b^{-1}; inverse precomposition preserves composition order and transports the Artin relators. This elementary passage is explicit in the outside gauge-covariance supplier but absent from this proof's restriction wording.

F2 states that the arbitrary subgroup Γ meets every nonempty open subset and cites the Fibonacci-specific density theorem. For the general Γ quantified in this lemma, that fact follows from the Given hypothesis that Γ is dense, rather than from the cited specialized theorem. The covering-sheet proof otherwise applies to the stated arbitrary Γ.

alerts.finding: lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension, Proof 1.2, fixes total d and says: 'Composing the child inclusions with an orthonormal basis of each V_{ef}^d gives orthogonal isometric inclusions of d into T. Their projections sum to id_T'. For fixed d this identity is false. In the supplied Fibonacci category, take T=τ⊗τ=1⊕τ and d=1: the indicated projection is the projection onto the unit summand and annihilates the nonzero τ summand, so it is not id_T. The fixed-total Hom-basis conclusion can still be obtained, but this resolution-of-identity sentence overstates what the fixed-d family supplies.
